quote: Well, I don’t think it would land very well. I think that it would confuse the voters. I think it would water down the effectiveness of the MLA that had to deal with that issue.
quote_react: create constituencies that would bite off a piece of Lethbridge and make it mixed with rural, how would that land with folks in this community or a similar community?
note: Rule 14: answer to Mr. Clark's question (quote_react is the commissioner's question). Presenter, a Lethbridge resident, also asks in his own statement that the commission 'maintain fair electoral boundaries that firmly delineate between the rural and urban areas' (EB-3). Does not say 'two districts'; direction only.

quote: I do worry that you could have four representatives from the city of Lethbridge.
quote_react: it is not lost on me, the last presenter, that we need to have a better relationship with the city of Lethbridge. But I do catch my breath when I see that diagram.
note: Reeve of MD of Taber reacting to the previous presenter's (Mr. Mills) four-riding diagram; Mr. Clark prompts 'You don’t like the four sort of . . .'. Worry is from the rural side (four MLAs tied to the city). No want for Lethbridge stated; later 'I’d like to keep it more rural' is about her own riding. Rejection only, so no majority code derives under section 5 (left null). No EB label precedes the quote in the record.

quote: restricting Lethbridge to having two representatives within the urban geographic boundaries and without outlying rural territories would accommodate for the population growth that Lethbridge has experienced
quote_react: what I would not understand is changing the electoral boundaries to add rural areas to the city of Lethbridge
note: Wrongly believed Coalhurst was in Lethbridge-West (corrected by Mr. Evans); request itself is clear.

quote: When you take part of a large urban centre to create a rurban, rural-urban, district, you fail to understand or respect the fact that the residents in both the urban and rural communities have different cultures
quote_react: the local norms and expectations for the people of Coalhurst or Picture Butte or Lethbridge county are different from the local norms and expectations for Lethbridge residents
note: Also: 'Lethbridge neither needs nor deserves another constituency'; and, to Mrs. Samson, that joining Coalhurst to Lethbridge 'definitely would rub them wrong'. Reacting to a rumoured third hybrid district. Does not literally say 'keep two city districts', hence direction. No EB label precedes the quote.

Local historian giving history: 'we have had a riding that has only been urban since 1909. We have never included rural areas since 1909, a long precedence for our community' and 13th Street as a natural east-west divider. Leans to L1 but is offered as context, with no request in the (abridged) record; rule 17, narrower code.

quote: Combining any part of the city of Lethbridge with the rural areas or smaller municipalities would really do nothing to ensure appropriate representation for residents of Lethbridge.
quote_react: There are four important reasons I’d like to highlight to maintain the boundaries for Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East.
note: MLA for Lethbridge-West. Wants the two city-only districts maintained; argues against 'rural-urban, or rurban, constituencies'.

quote: Lethbridge should maintain at least two constituencies which are entirely contained within the boundaries of the city of Lethbridge, so that map that’s displayed right there, that’s just fine with me
note: Argues against 'a riding that also includes big chunks of Lethbridge' with Coaldale, Coalhurst, Stirling, Raymond. No EB label in the record.

Reeve of Cardston County, about Cardston-Siksika. On Lethbridge-style mixing only: 'I have heard the talk here tonight of mixing rural and urban. I don’t know how I feel about that. I know that could work'. No stance.
Edmonton presenter; Lethbridge named only as a place she has visited ('From Alberta Beach to Valleyview to Lethbridge'). Her respect-city-limits argument is about Edmonton / general (HYBRID-GENERAL).
Edmonton MLA; speaks of Cardston-Siksika, Livingstone-Macleod and the Blackfoot nations (Piikani, Blood Tribe). City of Lethbridge never named.
St. Paul hearing, Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul. 'Lethbridge' occurs only in Mr. Clark's aside about where the commission had been; the presenter never names it.

quote: Red Deer, two seats; Lethbridge, two seats; Medicine Hat would have one seat and one hybrid seat
quote_react: where possible, keep seats contained within cities
note: Calgary & District Labour Council seat allocation; distinguishes full city seats from hybrid seats, and gives Lethbridge two full seats.
MLA for Banff-Kananaskis. Lethbridge named only in passing ('anything that is not Edmonton or Calgary or Lethbridge or Red Deer'); Livingstone-Macleod only re Eden Valley.
Airdrie resident; Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West cited as the model for two Airdrie-only districts (rule 6, comparison). No request about Lethbridge.

quote: Airdrie would stay the same at two, Lethbridge would stay the same at two, Medicine Hat would be incorporated as one
note: Calgary presenter's province-wide seat count. 'Stay the same at two' is the status quo for Lethbridge; he does not say the seats must lie inside the city, hence direction. Elsewhere argues generally against splitting an urban area and adding a rural part. No EB label precedes the quote.

quote: somebody made a presentation about splitting Lethbridge into four, going out into the related communities. As an MLA – again, I haven’t been an MLA in Lethbridge – that would seem to be a little untenable to serve those people.
quote_react: keep larger cities whenever possible within their own ridings, so cities like Medicine Hat, Airdrie, Lethbridge, Red Deer within their own riding or within two ridings if at all possible
note: Former Calgary MLA reacting to the four-way Lethbridge proposal made at the Lethbridge hearing ('That seems like a bad idea to me'). Closing remark (EB-278): 'Lethbridge is big enough that it should have as much of itself as its own riding as is humanly possible.' quote_react here carries the want.

Medicine Hat presenter arguing for blended ridings in general (HYBRID-GENERAL G-PRO: 'almost intentionally attach segments of city perimeters to rural districts'). Lethbridge comes up only as biography, a telecom market study, and having read the Lethbridge hearing transcript; no request about Lethbridge's districts.
Former Medicine Hat MLA on Medicine Hat ridings. Lethbridge named only as the hearing where someone cited Brooks-Medicine Hat; Taber as a separate regional community.
Medicine Hat presenter. 'water coming from the Lethbridge area' and Little Bow (2017 submitters) only; no stance on Lethbridge.
Brooks/Medicine Hat presenter. Lethbridge named only as a place Brooks-area people travel to for sport and shopping; wants Brooks with Taber. No stance on Lethbridge's districts.
Former Medicine Hat MLA. 'The Oldman River comes through Lethbridge' as geography only.
Peace River hearing. 'Lethbridge' occurs only in Mr. Evans's remark that he resides there; the presenter never names it.

quote: there might be a proposal to split up representation in Lethbridge into four hybrid ridings, basically partially rural and partially urban, and I’d like to speak against that proposal
quote_react: I think it’s important to maintain political representation for the city of Lethbridge that fully understands the complexity of the issues that a city like Lethbridge faces.
note: Former mayor of Lethbridge. Also (EB-404): 'I don’t see any advantage – in fact, I see significant disadvantages – to having blended hybrid MLAs representing the city.' No EB label precedes the main quote.

quote: I submit that Lethbridge needs to have its ridings within its own boundaries.
quote_react: If a hybrid district were to be implemented, it could place these groups in a situation where they may never see like-minded people running or winning a seat in the Legislature.
note: Lethbridge-East resident; allows that the east-west line inside the city may need adjusting.

quote: Treating the city of Lethbridge as a rural outpost or treating its surrounding agricultural lands as just another civic subdivision does not recognize their value. Urban and rural must be represented separately.
quote_react: Should northwest Lethbridge and the county feedlot operations, each with their attendant ancillary issues, be represented by one MLA, enormous pressure will be consistently applied to eliminate one or the other of the competing uses.
note: Former mayor of Lethbridge. Asked by Mrs. Samson whether he agrees with the current Lethbridge boundaries, answers 'it doesn’t make sense to change them from that perspective' (hedged). Exact rests on that answer plus the separate-representation request; a stricter reader could call it direction.
Foothills school division chair; Okotoks, Diamond Valley, Longview, Banff-Jasper. Livingstone-Macleod named as a riding only; Lethbridge never named.
Canmore presenter on Banff-Jasper and Cochrane-Springbank. Crowsnest Pass raised only by Mr. Clark; Lethbridge never named.

Medicine Hat presenter defending the two Medicine Hat hybrids. Names Lethbridge as a comparison city and, asked by Mr. Evans and the Chair about hybrids for Lethbridge, declines: 'As for Lethbridge, I can’t really comment on those areas' and 'I don’t think it’s a fair comparison that the model that works here will work there.' No stance on Lethbridge (rules 6 and 14).
Former Medicine Hat MLA. 'Lethbridge and Red Deer have two' (urban seats) offered as comparison for Medicine Hat's lack of one (rule 6). No request about Lethbridge.

quote: Dividing the city of Lethbridge into four urban-rural hybrid electoral divisions would not create a new regional structure; it would simply formalize the one that already governs southern Alberta in practice.
quote_react: the letter that I’d submitted respond directly to the commission’s request for further analysis on hybrid urban-rural electoral divisions in southern Alberta
note: Lethbridge resident, author of the four-way proposal made in round 1; responding to the interim report (which kept two city districts) and pressing his own plan (an IDEA at the time). Confirms to the Chair that a section of Lethbridge would go with the Crowsnest Pass ('I can and I do', EB-634) and that the plan makes six southern ridings of seven. No EB label precedes the main quote.
Medicine Hat presenter. Lethbridge named as a comparator that is afforded 'at least one fully urban riding' (rule 6). No request about Lethbridge.
Edmonton presenter; Lethbridge named only as a place he once practised. General objection to rural-urban ridings (HYBRID-GENERAL).
Edmonton-City Centre MLA. Livingstone-Macleod named only by Dr. Martin; Lethbridge never named.
Edmonton presenter on inner-city ridings; Taber-Warner and Manyberries as a comparison. Lethbridge never named.
Sherwood Park presenter. Lethbridge only as comparison: Sherwood Park under two MLAs 'the same way that the map is trying to do with Lethbridge' (rule 6).

Edmonton presenter. Lethbridge appears only inside her reading of the interim report ('One presenter from Southern Alberta insisted that Lethbridge be treated the same as Calgary and Edmonton'). Her scepticism about hybrids is about Calgary and Edmonton.

quote: I think that a hybrid of Lethbridge with more MLAs representing that city but also representing the areas that surround that city would be an effective way of doing it.
quote_react: an electoral district including areas of the city of Lethbridge, the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton Lakes national park, and the communities of Cardston, Magrath, Raymond, and Stirling would align well with the concept of effective representation
note: MLA for Cardston-Siksika. Describes hybrids radiating from the city (one west and south with Cardston and the Crowsnest Pass; Taber-Warner 'part of a hybrid Lethbridge riding of its own'), 'more than just two MLAs representing the third-largest city' (EB-826), and adopts the Chair's term in reply: 'this quad hybrid model' (EB-828). Never himself says 'four'; a stricter reader could call this direction. His single named district joins areas the minority map puts in two separate Lethbridge hybrids.

The presenter (Ms Al-Guneid, MLA Calgary-Glenmore) never names Lethbridge. Every Lethbridge passage in this record (after [EB-814]: 'Lethbridge will be better served with a quad hybrid system', Coaldale and Livingstone-Macleod) is spill-over from the next presenter, Mr. Hunter (MLA Taber-Warner), whom the Chair addresses by name; rule 14, only the presenter's own words count. If the adjudicator treats the spill-over as part of this record it would be L2 exact, but it belongs to Mr. Hunter's own appearance.
Lethbridge appears only in the form header (as the writer's place). Message is about rural versus urban riding populations province-wide; no request about Lethbridge's districts.
Cardston resident on the shape of Cardston-Siksika. Lethbridge not named.

Header municipality Lethbridge. Message is a general principle ('keeping urban and rural districts separate', 'municipal boundaries'), naming no place and not saying 'our city': HYBRID-GENERAL G-CON. Rules 1 and 17: no Lethbridge want coded, though it leans L1.

quote: have lived in Lethbridge (both East & West) since 2002 and believe the 2municipal election boundaries are ideal to maintain the midsized city as a cohesive entity
note: Header: Lethbridge East. '2municipal' is as OCR gives it (not corrected); read as the two ridings following the municipal boundary being ideal.
Medicine Hat and Brooks; Taber named once as comparison. Lethbridge not named.
Medicine Hat as one riding; Taber named once. Lethbridge not named.
Medicine Hat as one riding (near word for word EBC-2025-1-0058; campaign EBC-2025-1-0058). Lethbridge not named.

quote: If a blend of rural and city were to take place I'd be very concerned that the smaller rural community voices would feel lost in the voices of the city
quote_react: our needs are so much more aligned with the communities in the current riding that we are in, than they are with the people in the city
note: Coalhurst resident who works in Lethbridge; 'the city' is Lethbridge throughout. Rule 8 is met: she argues Coalhurst should not be blended with the city. She speaks for the rural side and does not say how the city's own seats should be drawn, hence direction; a narrower reader could code rejection only.

quote: I am writing to support the proposal to create four new electoral divisions (depicted in Annex A below) that more accurately reflect how southern Alberta is organized and connected.
note: Deputy Mayor of Coaldale. Names Lethbridge-Cardston, Lethbridge-Livingstone, Lethbridge-Little Bow, Lethbridge-Taber; Annex B (p. 5, low-confidence OCR, not quoted) splits the city's population four ways. Near-identical in design to the minority map.

quote: ensuring that electoral constituencies in Edmonton, Calgary, and other expanding municipalities, such as but not limited to Lethbridge, are housed exclusively inside municipal borders
note: Does not give a number of seats; asks for constituencies wholly inside the city, naming Lethbridge.

quote: For over 100 years the ridings of Lethbridge have been bound by the municipal boundary and I believe that is the way that it should remain.
quote_react: I would not want to see boundary lines drawn that meant the municipal boundary was not maintained for Lethbridge West and Lethbridge East.
note: Coalhurst resident who works in Lethbridge-West.

St. Albert-focused submission. Lethbridge named as a 'smaller regional centre' and as an example of a city with 'two wholly-urban ridings' / 'two stand-alone urban constituencies, like Lethbridge or Red Deer' (rule 6). General 'like with like' principle; no request about Lethbridge itself.

quote: Lethbridge is well served by the two current constituencies, Lethbridge West and Lethbridge East.
quote_react: The concerns of Lethbridge citizens are much different that the rural areas surrounding our city.
note: Lethbridge-East resident.

quote: Red Deer should have two seats. Lethbridge should have two seats. Medicine Hat should have a seat and a hybrid seat.
note: Calgary and District Labour Council. Seat table (p. 102) marks hybrid seats with an asterisk and gives Lethbridge 2/89 without one; hybrid seats are listed separately for Medicine Hat, Airdrie, St. Albert, Wood Buffalo. Pages 106 to 160 are the attached population-estimate tables (numbers only); read in part, scanned for prose.

quote: I propose replacing the current divisions of Cardston-Siksika, Livingstone-Macleod, Lethbridge-East, and Lethbridge-West with four new divisions
note: Cameron Mills (Lethbridge resident; Deputy CAO, Town of Coaldale): Lethbridge–Cardston, Lethbridge–Livingstone, Lethbridge–Little Bow, Lethbridge–Taber, with Annex B dividing the city's population four ways (pp. 192-193 low-confidence OCR, not quoted). Origin of the four-way plan; EBC-2025-1-0101 supports the same annexes.
Medicine Hat as one riding (attachment matches EBC-2025-1-0058 / 0068; campaign EBC-2025-1-0058). Taber named once; Lethbridge not named.

quote: Red Deer should have two seats. Lethbridge should have two seats. Medicine Hat should have a seat and a hybrid seat.
note: Edmonton and District Labour Council; same template and seat list as EBC-2025-1-0138 (campaign EBC-2025-1-0138). Table (pp. 7-8) marks hybrid seats with an asterisk; Lethbridge 2/89 has none.

quote: Maintain the 2 seats in Red Deer • Maintain the 2 seats in Lethbridge
note: Alberta Federation of Labour. Its table (p. 26) lists 'Lethbridge 2 Seats' beside 'Medicine Hat 1 Seat and 1 Hybrid Seat', so the two Lethbridge seats are non-hybrid.

Calgary-Shaw resident who once lived in Lethbridge West. Says his 'largest concern', 'having ties to St. Albert — Morinville as well as Lethbridge West', is the blending of city and rural ridings, but the only request is about Calgary-Shaw. Leans L1 / G-CON; no explicit request for Lethbridge (rule 17).

Lethbridge resident's critique of the criteria after the Lethbridge hearing. Notes the river as a possible Lethbridge East/West line and that municipal lines can be arbitrary for bedroom communities such as Coalhurst and Coaldale, but asks for no arrangement for Lethbridge.

quote: I should not be expected to drive nearly an hour to meet with an MLA whose constituency office is located in a region I have no ties to, when the city that shapes every aspect of my life—Lethbridge—is represented by a different MLA altogether.
quote_react: The new proposed boundaries move me into Livingstone—Macleod, another region that does not represent the community of interest I actually belong to.
note: Lives 'just outside the City of Lethbridge—only a two-minute drive from the city limits' and wants her peri-urban area represented with the city, not with Cardston-Siksika or Livingstone-Macleod. That is a joining of adjacent country to a city riding, not hybrid ridings as a design, hence L3. Geometry: she does not say which side of the city; if west of the Oldman River, the majority map's small Lethbridge County addition to Lethbridge-West may cover her.

quote: we need MLA representation that reflects and strengthens that rural influence. Please reconsider your first plans by keeping just two fully urban seats for Lethbridge
note: Header: Lethbridge-East; issues ticked include 'Hybrid electoral divisions'. The last sentence is ambiguous: read with the argument, it asks the commission to reconsider its plan of keeping just two fully urban seats (so rural influence in Lethbridge's seats); read literally it could ask to keep two urban seats (L1). Coded on the argument; adjudicator should look.

quote: Lethbridge warrants at least two dedicated electoral districts to reflect its size, diversity, and continued growth.
quote_react: the proposal to divide it into four districts that incorporate significant rural territories is deeply worrisome
note: Reacting to the four-way proposal (on no map at the time), not to the interim map, which kept two city seats. 'I respectfully call on the Commission to reject any proposal that divides Lethbridge into rural-urban ridings'. Reads like a template letter; first of its kind in this unit.

quote: it feels as though an opportunity was wasted when not expanding the City's representation past its borders into the County. Hybrid electoral divisions could serve to breakdown many of the rural/urban divisions we find ourselves battling
note: Reeve, on behalf of Lethbridge County Council. Asks for the city's representation to extend into the county through hybrid divisions; gives no number of ridings. Also wants the county's riding to stretch east, not west and north.
Central Alberta ridings. Lethbridge named only as a place where a hearing was held.
Mackenzie County resident on northern ridings; Cardston-Siksika named once as an example of rural boundary shifts. Lethbridge not named.
Medicine Hat resident asking for a fully urban Medicine Hat division. Lethbridge is a comparator ('leaving Lethbridge fully urban', 'Grande Prairie, Lethbridge, and Red Deer'); rule 6.

quote: it is good that our overall urban community remains as two urban ridings, without being lumped together with smaller nearby communities, or having our community's representation diluted by being chopped up into more ridings
note: Lethbridge resident. Main request is about the east-west line inside the city (12th or 13th Street; attached map p. 24, low-confidence OCR, shows that internal line only).

quote: The “perfect” number for two constituencies is 109,858 or within 1.5%, making Lethbridge an ideal candidate for two urban constituencies.
quote_react: am fully supportive of the proposals of your interim report respecting those constituencies dated October 2025
note: Former mayor of Lethbridge (listed as former councillor). Argues against the model 'which combines the two rational city constituencies into four hybrid city and rural constituencies' (p. 126) and ends 'Urban and rural must be represented separately' (p. 130).

quote: I’m very satisfied with the outcome (especially vis a vis the traditional Lethbridge electoral boundaries) and with the recommendations of this report
quote_react: I argued (somewhat obliquely) to maintain the City of Lethbridge’s traditional electoral boundaries and against so-called hybrid representation
note: Same person as HANSARD-R1-T01-001. Recalls having argued against hybrids but reflects that his historical analogy may have been the wrong one, so no rejection coded here.

quote: I also appreciate how you stayed true to the 116-year old precedent that guides the Lethbridge ridings by staying solely within the boundary of the City of Lethbridge with the borders of these two constituencies.
note: Local historian (same person as HANSARD-R1-T02-007); here the approval of city-only ridings is explicit.

quote: I would like to commend the commission on making the recommendation that Lethbridge KEEPS it current consistencies of Lethbridge East and Lethbridge West.
quote_react: What is important to me is that we do not dilute urban concerns and needs with the desires of the rural constituencies that surround us.
note: 'consistencies' as written (constituencies).
Carseland (Wheatland County) resident. 'County of Lethbridge border' is only the far edge of a proposed riding; the City of Lethbridge is not discussed.

quote: I encourage the boundary commission to reconsider the four-quadrant hybrid model for Lethbridge.
quote_react: The hybrid model embeds that interdependence into representation, aligning policy accountability with where water related outcomes are felt.
note: Lethbridge County resident; header lists Lethbridge East, Lethbridge West, Livingstone-Macleod, Taber-Warner. 'Reconsider' = take up again the model the interim report set aside. Phrase 'four-quadrant hybrid' recurs in EBC-2025-2-0438; likely campaign wording.

Fort Macleod resident objecting to Coaldale and Lethbridge County in Livingstone-Macleod ('a Lethbridge commuters riding'). Rule 8: says nothing in words about how the city is divided. Attached map opened (source PDF p. 73): it draws Lethbridge as two districts inside the city and puts Coaldale in a separate rural district to the east and south. That is consistent with L1 but the map is offered for the rural ridings, so no want coded; an adjudicator could accept L1 'from map'.

quote: I strongly encourage the adoption of a four-quadrant hybrid approach for the Lethbridge region.
quote_react: A hybrid model that thoughtfully distributes urban neighbourhoods while preserving rural communities more accurately reflects the real movement patterns of families and young people throughout the region.
note: Raymond resident. Shares the 'four-quadrant hybrid' wording with EBC-2025-2-0422 (campaign wording, texts otherwise differ).

quote: I am writing to express my support for maintaining the current electoral boundaries in the ridings of Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West.
quote_react: Dividing these boundaries would risk diluting the urban voice by subsuming it within surrounding rural communities
note: Lethbridge-West resident.

Coaldale resident asking that Coaldale stay in its current district (Taber-Warner), on the strength of its corridor ties to Lethbridge and Taber. Rule 8: does not say Coaldale should share a district with part of the city. Near-identical argument to the Mayor's letter EBC-2025-2-0535 (campaign EBC-2025-2-0535; same surname).

quote: I appreciate that the Commission largely kept the boundaries of Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West the same, and did not split the city into four to include outlying rural areas.
note: Edmonton resident who grew up in Lethbridge.

quote: Edmonton, Calgary, Lethbridge and other urban ridings should remain within the city and not extend into surrounding communities.
note: Edmonton resident; Lethbridge named in the request itself.

Fort Macleod resident with a business in Lethbridge. Wants boundary changes 'to bridge the gap between urban and rural interests', which leans toward a Lethbridge hybrid, but never says Lethbridge should be joined to country ridings. Rule 17: no want; HYBRID-GENERAL G-PRO.

Mayor of Coaldale for Town Council: keep Coaldale in Taber-Warner, in the Highway 3 corridor 'anchored by Lethbridge'. Rule 8: no statement that Coaldale should share a district with part of the city, or on how the city is divided.
Mayor of Coalhurst: keep Coalhurst's current boundary, against the westward Livingstone-Macleod. The City of Lethbridge is never named.

quote: The four quadrant hybrid meets each criterion more precisely than the status quo.
quote_react: quadrant alignment offers that stability without diminishing rural seats. Therefore, the hybrid model is not merely preferable—it is the option that most directly fulfills the Commission’s statutory mandate
note: Coaldale resident (a Coaldale councillor by the cc list on EBC-2025-2-0535). 'Four quadrant hybrid' wording as in EBC-2025-2-0422 and 0438; corridor paragraph echoes the Coaldale letters. Campaign wording, first seen EBC-2025-2-0422.

quote: I appreciate that you took the submission of historians like Belinda Crowson seriously and maintained the municipal boundary to these ridings.
note: Coalhurst resident (same writer as EBC-2025-1-0119). Thanks the commission for not merging her rural neighbours 'with urban ridings' and finds Livingstone-Macleod reasonable; also proposes Highway 3 as the line between the two city ridings.

quote: I am writing to express my support for maintaining the current Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East constituencies as outlined in the Interim Report.
note: Lethbridge-West resident. Adds that the configuration 'reflects established communities of interest and existing municipal boundaries'.
Canmore resident proposing a Canmore-Crowsnest Pass division (CANMORE-JASPER J5). Lethbridge not named.

quote: I see no downside to having 4 MLAs to represent Lethbridge in combination with the surrounding rural area.
quote_react: Four voices at the table as opposed to two will benefit Lethbridge and its rural neighbors dramatically.
note: Lethbridge-West resident.

quote: Splitting Lethbridge into four rural-urban ridings does not make good sense, in my view.
quote_react: I hope the recommendations from the Interim Report will be maintained in the final submission.
note: Lethbridge-West resident; quotes the interim report's finding that the two Lethbridge divisions are 'clearly logical' and agrees. Accepts hybrids elsewhere 'where they might be necessary'.
Northern MLAs' proposal (Lesser Slave Lake and the north); supports more hybrids in the Edmonton and Calgary regions. 'Crowsnest Pass' occurs only in the quoted statute. Lethbridge not named.

quote: By dividing Lethbridge interests across three constituencies—West, East, and a North-Hybrid—the Commission will provide Southern Albertans with a legislative voice commensurate with their economic contribution
quote_react: This allows CTW to absorb the northern portion of the City of Lethbridge. This creates a third Lethbridge-focused MLA through an urban-rural hybrid model
note: Three seats: two city seats plus one hybrid (north Lethbridge joined to Cardston-Taber-Warner). Particulars contradict the four-way plan, so L3 under rule 7; on neither final map. Writer argues the merit of urban-rural hybrids in general terms too.

quote: A district that links parts of Lethbridge with the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton Lakes National Park, and Cardston, Magrath, Raymond, and Stirling would accurately reflect how southern Albertans live and interact.
note: Lethbridge-West resident; header names Cardston-Taber-Warner. Asks for a hybrid joining parts of the city to the south-west, with no number of ridings and nothing on the rest of the city. Same argument, in the same order, as Mr. Schow's testimony (HANSARD-R2-T47-003) and EBC-2025-2-0682: campaign, first in this unit. The one district named spans two of the minority's four hybrids; a stricter reader could code L3.

quote: A district that unites portions of Lethbridge with the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton Lakes National Park, and the communities of Cardston, Magrath, Raymond, and Stirling would do precisely that.
note: Cardston County resident; ticks 'Hybrid electoral divisions'. campaign EBC-2025-2-0678 (paragraph for paragraph the same argument, reworded). Same caveat: one hybrid district named, no four-way particulars.

quote: Lethbridge should not be divided into 4.
note: Entire message (7 words, under the 8-word floor; nothing longer exists). Header: Lethbridge-West resident writing about Lethbridge-West. Rejection of the four-way plan is exact; the want (leave the city's two seats) is inferred, hence direction.

quote: Don't touch the electoral boundaries. What's wrong with your people? Rural and urban concerns are completely different. Leave them alone.
note: Entire message. Lethbridge is named only in the header (municipality Lethbridge; current and target division Lethbridge-East), used under rule 2. Reads as: keep Lethbridge's boundaries and keep rural and urban apart.

quote: A splitting of Lethbridge into four ridings and including the surrounding rural areas seems to be not only ineffective in conveying a realistic portrayal of the population, but detrimental to the citizens within the City of Lethbridge and the surrounding area.
quote_react: I’m happy and thankful the commission has preliminarily chosen to maintain the integrity and history associated with Lethbridge in two
note: Lethbridge-East resident. The sentence in quote_react continues on p. 3: 'ridings by maintaining the current municipal boundary.' Reacts also to 'the electoral boundary proposal submitted by my MLA and members of the Town of Coaldale'.

Medicine Hat resident asking for a single urban Medicine Hat riding. Notes that 'the idea of splitting Lethbridge into four sections' was discussed in the media and that this 'raises broader concerns about [...] the potential normalization of dividing cohesive urban communities'. Disapproving, but offered as evidence for her Medicine Hat case, not as a request about Lethbridge; rule 17. An adjudicator could accept rejects = L2.
Entire message: 'Urban and Rural Alberta both deserve fair representation.' Header: Lethbridge-East. No arrangement asked for.

quote: Please leave Lethbridge’s boundaries as they are currently written
note: Entire message. Header: Lethbridge-East resident. 'As they are currently written' = the two city districts in force.
Calgary-Hays resident; Lethbridge only as a place he has lived. Request is about Calgary-Hays (no rural areas added).

quote: Lethbridge needs another seat just for itself, it should not include rural districts around it.
note: L9 = a further seat wholly inside the city (three city-only seats), on no map. Clearly against any joining of city and country. An adjudicator may prefer L1 at direction (city-only seats), which would make the majority code 2 instead of 4; 'another seat just for itself' is the obstacle.

quote: I am generally in agreement that the ridings of Lethbridge East and West should NOT be split into 4 separate ridings, incorporating several rural corridors.
note: Lethbridge-West resident agreeing with the interim report.

quote: Lethbridge does not need to be divided into four electoral regions which would include large areas of rural ridings. We are a small city and are easily managed by two MLAs.
note: Lethbridge-East resident.

quote: I don't believe it is wise to split Lethbridge into 4 ridings. It would be difficult for a MLA to represent the diverse interests of those in the City of Lethbridge and those in the surrounding rural communities.
note: Lethbridge-East resident. Rejection of the four-way plan is exact; the want (separate urban and rural MLAs) is direction, as she does not say 'two city seats'.

quote: I don't feel there is a need to redraw the electoral districts at this time. This seems overtly political and unethical.
note: Entire message. Lethbridge named only in the header (Lethbridge-West resident writing about Lethbridge-West; 'Hybrid electoral divisions' ticked), used under rule 2. Read as: leave Lethbridge's districts as they are. Could fairly be coded mention only.

quote: Please leave Lethbridge in the current boundaries. We do NOT want any changes.
note: Lethbridge-East resident.

quote: I agree with the commission's opinion that Lethbridge should not be divided up into four ridings
note: Edmonton resident writing about Lethbridge-West. Entire message; agrees with the interim report's refusal of the four-way plan. Want inferred from agreement with the commission, hence direction.

quote: was pleased to see that the proposed boundary amendments for Lethbridge advised only minor adjustments within the city limits. This approach best supports effective representation for both Lethbridge and the surrounding area.
quote_react: Some of the proposals presented in the first round of submissions awkwardly suggested merging rural and urban ridings in Lethbridge and southern Alberta, effectively blurring the municipal boundary of Lethbridge.
note: Lethbridge-West resident. 'the Commission’s decision not to advance this approach is welcome'.

quote: As a solution, I support the Lethbridge quad hybrid model.
quote_react: it would give Lethbridge double the MLAs to advocate for their needs compared to the current two
note: MD of Taber resident. Also wants one Taber constituency running from Lethbridge County east to Bow Island along Highway 3. 'Quad hybrid' is the term used at the MLA hearing (HANSARD-R2-T47-003).

quote: I am happy with the current electoral boundaries for Lethbridge East and Lethbridge West as they serve an Urban area and the City of Lethbridge the best.
note: Lethbridge-East resident. 'Keep the electoral boundaries as the are!'

quote: A district that unites portions of Lethbridge with the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton Lakes National Park, and the communities of Cardston, Magrath, Raymond, and Stirling would meaningfully reflect southern Alberta as it exists today
note: campaign EBC-2025-2-0678 (same argument paragraph for paragraph; shares a surname with that writer). Lethbridge-West resident; ticks 'Hybrid electoral divisions'. One hybrid district named, no four-way particulars; a stricter reader could code L3.

quote: is to emphasize the infeasibility of the proposed endeavour to conjoin rural and urban electoral constituencies in Southern Alberta
quote_react: I suggest that putting rural and urban constituencies together in one demographic basket will seriously test the ability of any individual MLA to do the job they were elected to do.
note: Lethbridge-East resident; header target: 'merging of urban and rural electoral boundaries in southern alberta'. She writes of 'Southern Alberta' and 'the example of Lethbridge', never 'Lethbridge's ridings' in so many words; place taken from header and context (rule 2). Writes as if the merger were the commission's proposal; it was a submitted idea. Want (keep urban and rural apart) is direction.

quote: Take, for example, the submission made arguing for highly tormented ridings, collecting much of rural Lethbridge area in four ridings connecting like a pie to the city. These arguments are clearly partisan in nature
quote_react: we commend the Commission’s overall approach to communities of interest in the interim report, and recommend a stronger adherence to non-hybrid ridings
note: Public Interest Alberta (Edmonton). Rejection of the four-way Lethbridge plan is exact; the want is general ('non-hybrid ridings') and applied to Lethbridge by the example, hence direction.

quote: I strongly oppose making Lethbridge West a rural–urban hybrid riding.
quote_react: the latest suggested boundary from the commission for Lethbridge-West is acceptable to me. It preserves the urban character of the riding
note: Lethbridge-West resident. 'I respectfully urge the Commission to maintain an urban-focused Lethbridge-West'.

quote: I am writing to express my support for maintaining the current Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East constituencies as outlined in the Interim Report.
note: campaign EBC-2025-2-0635 (near word for word). Lethbridge-West resident.

Northern package from the MLA for Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul (35 pages): his Bonnyville proposal plus the joint northern MLAs' paper already read in full under EBC-2025-2-0669. Lethbridge is not named; 'Crowsnest Pass' occurs only in the quoted statute. Cover letter and first proposal read; the rest searched for Lethbridge, southern Alberta and hybrid passages, not read line by line.

quote: I was happy to see that the proposed maps don't seem to have the 'cracking' and 'packing' that you see there, despite the worrying suggestion that it be done to Lethbridge.
note: Calgary resident. Rejects the suggested splitting of Lethbridge as US-style cracking; want (leave Lethbridge as the interim map has it) is implied by approval of the map, hence direction. Otherwise a general anti-hybrid letter (G-CON).

quote: Lethbridge is a regional city centre and a key hub for farming services and businesses; constituency boundaries should not be limited to city boundaries.
quote_react: Elections Alberta should be redrawing Lethbridge and rural area boundaries to accommodate rapid city and adjacent rural growth
note: Lethbridge-West resident. Wants Lethbridge constituencies to reach past the city limits as a matter of design, with relatives just outside the city put 'in Lethbridge-East and/or in a new additional constituency'. No number of ridings and nothing like four radiating districts; a stricter reader could code L3.

Entire message: 'Division is not necessary.' Header: Lethbridge-East resident writing about Lethbridge-East. Probably means the city need not be divided (against the four-way plan), but four words cannot carry it; rule 17. Adjudicator could accept rejects = L2.
Big Lakes County resident against representation by population. 'Crowsnest Pass' as an example of a distant place; Lethbridge not named.

quote: I am advocating for Lethbridge being broken into 4 ridings that have rural components.
quote_react: Lethbridge is an Agri-hub for the corridor and should be represented as such politically.
note: County of Lethbridge business owner; also wants Coaldale kept in Taber-Warner, not Livingstone-Macleod (OCR/spelling 'Tabor Warner', 'Livingston McLeod' in the original).

quote: Leave Lethbridge as is.
note: Entire message (4 words, under the 8-word floor; nothing longer exists). Header: Lethbridge-West resident writing about Lethbridge-West. 'As is' = the two city districts.
Edmonton-Riverview constituency manager on Edmonton. Lethbridge only in a statistical comparison ('Lethbridge, Airdrie, and Red Deer have no 5+ percentage point variance ridings'); rule 6.

quote: I am writing a proposal for an electoral district that includes parts of the City of Lethbridge, the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton Lakes National Park, and the surrounding southern Alberta communities.
note: campaign EBC-2025-2-0678 (same district, same three reasons, in a student's voice). Lethbridge-West; ticks 'Hybrid electoral divisions'. One hybrid district; no four-way particulars.

quote: consider a hybrid rural-urban model for the Lethbridge region by adjusting the Lethbridge ridings so that some immediately adjacent, strongly connected communities and county areas are included with Lethbridge—rather than keeping the city almost entirely isolated inside two urban-only divisions
note: Lethbridge-West resident. Argues the interim structure, which 'keeps Lethbridge as two mostly urban-only ridings', does not give fair representation. Asks for a hybrid model as a design, without a number of ridings; her 'immediately adjacent' wording is closer to L3 than to four far-reaching districts, so a stricter reader could code L3.

MLA for Fort McMurray-Lac La Biche: the joint northern MLAs' paper (read in full under EBC-2025-2-0669), here pasted into the form and attached again, with northern maps. Lethbridge is not named; 'Crowsnest Pass' occurs only in the quoted statute. Opening read; the rest searched for Lethbridge and southern Alberta passages, not read line by line.

St. Albert resident. Lethbridge only as the benchmark of a city large enough for 'two urban seats' / 'two wholly-urban ridings like those two cities do already' (rule 6). Request concerns St. Albert, Medicine Hat, Airdrie, Fort McMurray.

quote: Please maintain your recommendations for Lethbridge in your final report.
quote_react: The blatantly obvious attempt to manipulate electoral boundaries in Lethbridge by splitting the city into corners.
note: Lethbridge-East resident. Calls 'a proposal to split Lethbridge up into three or four ridings' political opportunism and compares Red Deer.

quote: I new model of hybrid rural-urban ridings to enhance representation of the local population and economic drivers would help.
quote_react: Fair representation should give Lethbridge a more significant voice. Many people live outside the city, but work within it or vice versa.
note: Lethbridge-West resident. 'I new model' as written. Hybrid ridings for Lethbridge as a design, with more MLAs; no number given.

quote: I like the proposal about splitting up Lethbridge into 4 ridings.
quote_react: I wouldn't be concerned about hybrid districts that have a mix of rural and urban. I think it's good.
note: Stirling resident. In the header he names the four districts he is writing about: 'Lethbridge-Fort Macleod, Lethbridge-Taber-Warner, Lethbridge-Cardston, Lethbridge-Little Bow' (p. 67), which are the names the minority map later used.

quote: I hope that the boundaries of Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East that have been proposed make it to the final submission. Not only does it follow major roads, and respects municipal boundaries
note: Lethbridge resident (province-wide alternative map, 30 pages, read in full). Keeps 'double-urban Lethbridge' and proposes a rural Coaldale-Cardston riding wrapped around the city that 'would respect both the differences of norms and expectations from and proximity to Lethbridge' (p. 101).

MLA for Cypress-Medicine Hat defending the two Medicine Hat hybrids. Lethbridge only as a comparison ('more direct representation per capita than cities like Red Deer, Lethbridge, Airdrie, and Grande Prairie'); rule 6.

from map. Canmore resident asking for a Canmore-Crowsnest Pass riding (CANMORE-JASPER J5); the text never names Lethbridge. The attached map (source PDF p. 180, opened) is a photograph of a prepared district sheet titled 'NEW: 64 EASTERN SLOPES', with neighbouring districts labelled '75 LETHBRIDGE-FORT MACLEOD' and '74 LETHBRIDGE-CARDSTON' and a line 'Potential Voter Outcome: 58%'. The Lethbridge hybrids appear only as neighbours' labels on someone's wider plan, not as this writer's request: mention, no want. Worth an adjudicator's and the audit's attention as evidence that a full four-Lethbridge-hybrid map was circulating by 18 December 2025.

quote: I therefore request greater representation, to encompass Lethbridge and also its surrounding bedroom communities. There was a previous proposal to do this. It needs to be revisited, and maybe reworked.
quote_react: the representation of two MLAs for Lethbridge is no longer sufficient
note: Lethbridge-West resident; ticks only 'Hybrid electoral divisions'. Points back to the earlier (four-way) proposal but allows it to be 'reworked', so direction. Also objects to London Road moving wholly into Lethbridge-East.

quote: please reconsider the introduction of hybrid districts around our urban centres - Calgary, Edmonton, Lethbridge, Red Deer, etc. Creating new mixed districts of urban+rural populations is a disservice to both.
note: Calgary-Klein resident. Lethbridge is named in a list of cities that should have no hybrid districts; no particulars for Lethbridge, hence direction. (The interim map proposed no Lethbridge hybrid; she is objecting to hybrids as such.)

quote: I appreciate the Commission's attention to keeping Lethbridge-West and Lethbridge-East fairly regular with their previous boundaries.
quote_react: dividing our city into semi-rural/semi-urban ridings would only serve to dilute not only the urban voters and their concerns, but those of the rural voters
note: Lethbridge-West resident.
St. Albert resident. Lethbridge only as the benchmark of a city with 'two ridings like Red Deer or Lethbridge' (rule 6). Shares its argument with EBC-2025-2-0993.

quote: I have read the interim report for this area and I appreciate the work put into it and the recommendations within it.
note: Entire message. 'This area' is Lethbridge-East by the header (municipality Lethbridge; current and target division Lethbridge-East), rule 2. Approval of the interim recommendations there is a want for what they are (rule 5), stated without particulars.

quote: I support the interim recommendation that Lethbridge stays as 2 electoral ridings with the boundaries in the city.
quote_react: Having more than 2 electoral riding within Lethbridge is no needed at all.
note: Lethbridge-East resident. First of a matching pair with EBC-2025-2-1125.

quote: I support the interim recommendation that Lethbridge stays as 2 electoral ridings with the boundaries in the city.
note: campaign EBC-2025-2-1119 (first two sentences near word for word). Lethbridge-West resident.

quote: I am writing to voice my support maintaining the current electoral boundaries in the ridings of Lethbridge-East and Lethbridge-West.
quote_react: By maintaining the current boundaries, and adding an additional seat in Lethbridge to reflect our growing population, we can continue to meet each the unique needs of both rural and city without pitting us against one another.
note: Lethbridge-West resident; opening and closing follow the template of EBC-2025-2-0441 (campaign EBC-2025-2-0441). Coded on the stated request to maintain the two city ridings; she also asks for 'an additional seat in Lethbridge' (a third city seat, on no map), which an adjudicator could treat as L9 as in EBC-2025-2-0733. 'Forcing disparate groups into one riding serves neither group.'

quote: By proposing to change the electoral boundaries to include more rural representation in Urban areas you dilute the urban voice and skew representation towards the UCP.
quote_react: DO NOT Change the Lethbridge electoral boundaries!!!
note: Lethbridge-West resident. Writes as if the hybrid plan were the commission's or the government's proposal; the interim map kept the two city seats. quote_react carries the want.
